architecture.tierEnd2: IoU pseudo-tracking: crop only on enter / significant pose change / exit
architecture.tierEdge1: Receives 450 QPS capture thumbnails over HTTP/MQTT, skipping decode
architecture.tierEdge4: Concurrently matches against an in-memory watchlist at millisecond latency
architecture.tierCloud2: Real-time KNN by day; GPU graph clustering 02:00–05:00
architecture.tierCloud4: 24h of hot data in VRAM; cold data sinks to the business center
architecture.spec_bw_detail: IPC → street node, 0.18 Mbps per camera
architecture.spec_cost_detail: Full-system deployment cost (excluding existing pure storage)
architecture.dcComputeRoleV: 15,000 QPS vector writes, CAGRA retrieval, GPU graph clustering
architecture.dcBusinessRoleV: NVR video storage, business APIs, auth/logs, Mamba training, full cold archive
architecture.dcComputeDataV: Hot vectors for IDs unmerged within 24h (memory / GPU VRAM)
architecture.dcBusinessDataV: Historical footage + permanent vectors and track archives for IDs merged beyond 24h
architecture.dcBusinessNetV: 10 GbE private line intake, security private network, public business APIs
architecture.sched1_desc: All IPC video streams straight to the business-center NVR; capture thumbnails go to street nodes for embedding; business lookups over <24h query the compute center with a 128-d KNN, independent of unmerged temporary IDs.
architecture.sched2_desc: Flush and persist: the compute center triggers a vector-store Flush(), moving in-memory segments into the binlog.
architecture.sched3_desc: GPU graph clustering: 32 GPUs are isolated to run spatiotemporally pruned union-find and Louvain over the day's 130M vectors, deriving Global_Person_ID.
architecture.sched4_desc: Incremental sync: about 1.5 GB of the vector / Global_ID / spatiotemporal index is pushed to the business center, after which data older than 24 hours is erased.
architecture.rackC: Class C control ×4 · 4×3.84 TB NVMe RAID10
architecture.mambaExplain: When appearance is highly similar (S_visual = 0.92) but the cross-camera spatiotemporal transition is implausible (S_mamba = 0.02), the final score drops to 0.018 and the candidate is rejected as a false positive.
architecture.coldStartTitle: Cold-start data augmentation for new checkpoints
architecture.coldGeomMaskV: Randomly mask 20–30% of intermediate checkpoint nodes, forcing the model to learn physical spatial continuity
architecture.coldRoadPathV: Generate synthetic trajectories from the OSM road network and speed limits for pretraining
architecture.wlBroadcastV: Pulsar/Kafka compacted topic; edge and cloud subscription updates complete within 50 ms
architecture.wlGemmV: Watchlist vectors stay resident in VRAM as a matrix; a single comparison takes < 0.5 ms
architecture.wlEdgeV: Local SIMD matching against a 2.5 MB watchlist; on a hit, MQTT pushes straight to the field terminal in 50–100 ms
architecture.wlDebounceV: A 5-minute sliding window over Watchlist_ID + Camera_ID; a tombstone revokes network-wide in 10 ms
architecture.wlLatencyV: 50 ms express alert at the edge / 200 ms global alert from the cloud
architecture.gwSceneAV: Route to the compute center, run Milvus/CAGRA nearest-neighbour retrieval, return in milliseconds
architecture.gwSceneB: Scenario B · older than 24 hours only
architecture.gwSceneBV: Query the business center directly; if a Global_Person_ID exists, look it up in SQL/ES, otherwise query the local historical vector cold store
architecture.gwSceneC: Scenario C · joint query across 24 hours
architecture.gwSceneCV: Concurrently query both sides, then sort by timestamp, drop anomalous spatiotemporal noise, and stitch the full track
architecture.gatewayFootnote: The api.py in this demo implements a prototype of that gateway: it hides backbone / vector-store details from callers, but has only one data center, no Mamba pruning, and no historical cold-store branch.
architecture.opsBufferV: Street nodes carry 512 GB NVMe as a ring buffer, caching 48 hours of vectors locally during outages and resuming upload afterwards
architecture.opsHaV: Multi-replica Milvus; a Class C control node failure fails over within 3 seconds; MinIO EC 6+2 tolerates 2 simultaneous disk losses
architecture.opsOtaV: All compute units are packaged as Docker images and managed by K3s (edge) and K8s (cloud), supporting canary rollouts and seamless rolling upgrades
architecture.k8sMention: All compute units are containerized and orchestrated by K3s (edge) / K8s (cloud) — see the K8s Orchestration tab.

map.demoDetail: The basemap is live (Tencent Maps GL JS), but the camera ledger is still simulated by a local config file and is not wired to a real device-management platform (RTSP / GB28181 / ONVIF); status columns all show "Not connected". This project is a feasibility study only — parts of the code are carried over and do not represent the final system.
map.basemapNote: Basemap: Tencent Maps GL JS (official CDN + local key proxy; no plaintext key in the front end). CRS: GCJ-02. Pan/zoom is handled by the SDK.
map.ledgerSource: The config file is simulated data used to demo map rendering and track chaining; coordinates are approximate positions near public roads and do not represent real checkpoint deployments.

map.apiList: Return the full camera and edge-node ledger
map.apiDetail: Detail and latest report for a single device

map.complianceSubtitle: Basemap source must be on the whitelist
map.complianceNote: Overseas basemaps (Google / Apple / Bing overseas / OSM direct / Mapbox / Leaflet+OSM) are prohibited.
map.compliance1: Allowed: Tencent Maps / AMap / Baidu Maps / Tianditu
map.compliance3: No military restricted zones or classified coordinates
map.compliance4: Point data must comply with the Personal Information Protection Law
map.complianceKeyNote: Integration: the SDK loads from the official CDN; the key is held by the back-end proxy, never exposed in plaintext on the front end.
map.trackNote: Once implemented, the Smart Gateway merges "compute-center KNN results + business-center archive", sorts by timestamp, and drops spatiotemporally noisy points before drawing.

k8s.demoDetail: This demo runs as a single Python process with no containerization and no Kubernetes cluster. The workload list below comes from the design goals in docs/SYSTEM.md and shows the planned shape. This project is a feasibility study only — parts of the code are carried over and do not represent the final system.
k8s.panelSubtitle: docs/SYSTEM.md core principle 5 · cloud-edge consistent deployment and scheduling
k8s.panelBody: Every compute unit on the edge nodes and in the compute center is packaged as a standard Docker image and managed centrally by Kubernetes (K3s at the edge, K8s in the cloud), enabling cloud-edge consistent deployment, canary releases, and elastic scaling.
k8s.roleCluster: GPU graph clustering at 02:15 (cuGraph union-find + Louvain)
k8s.apiNote: GET /api/k8s/workloads and POST /api/k8s/rollout are already defined and callable; ready replicas and cluster metrics fill in once a K3s/K8s cluster is connected.
k8s.imageSubtitle: Cloud-edge consistent registry and version alignment
k8s.imageNote: Canary releases rely on immutable image tags plus cross-cluster version comparison.
k8s.rolloutSubtitle: One-click rollout when swapping the Re-ID model or Mamba engine
k8s.rolloutNote: SYSTEM.md §9.3: one-click canary rollout with seamless rolling upgrades from the cloud.
